title: Readiness Leakage Validation — Board E
type: Read-Only Readiness Validation — No Content Modifications
authority: S350 Readiness Scorecard (Board C); S204 Readiness Results (Board E); SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24.md; CURRENT_BASELINES.md
purpose: Compare current readiness distribution against 89.5% v1 baseline. Measure leakage from known-defect QIDs in the Certified pool.

evidence.domain_e_seeds: 34 of 38 Domain E seeds arrived at certification with 2+ concurrent defects
evidence.zero_scanned: 38 of 38 seeds had zero pre-certification automated scanning
evidence.preventable_pct: 91.5% of leakage events preventable via pre-flight gating

current_readiness_distribution.source: S322 live scan (scripts/output/readiness_scoring.json) — most recent operational data
current_readiness_distribution.analysis: Of 2,540 items: 242 are structurally BLOCKED (identity, JSON integrity, or severe structural defects), 77 require REMEDIATION (DL-008, DL-026, DL-016), 2,221 are CERTIFIED. Zero items are in READY state — items bypassed the readiness gate because v2 board visibility rules are not yet active.

per_domain_readiness.analysis: Domains B, C, D fully ready. Domain A nearly ready (99.47%). Domains E and F are readiness drag (~60%) — these contain uncertified sections with structural defects holding items in BLOCKED and REMEDIATE states.

certified_pool_defect_leakage.description: Known defects in the active Certified learner pool (2,221 items). These are leakage events — items that reached Certified status with undetected defects.

DL-021_Pack_E_Section_C_absent_EW.scope: All Pack E Section C items (P1E-C-001 through P1E-C-100). 5 previously remediated in Autonomous Run Part 4. 95 remain.
DL-021_Pack_E_Section_C_absent_EW.learner_impact: Learners receive no distractor feedback on incorrect answers for Section C items. Degraded educational experience.
DL-021_Pack_E_Section_C_absent_EW.leakage_source: Template pipeline gap — per-section flag suppressed distractor ExplanationWrong generation. Items were certified without distractor explanations.

DL-016_Pack_A_metadata_offset.scope: Pack A Section E + all Pack A sections with dual-block architecture. ExplanationWrong fields describe wrong item's distractors.
DL-016_Pack_A_metadata_offset.learner_impact: Learners may see distractor explanations about a completely different topic. Learner-safety risk.
DL-016_Pack_A_metadata_offset.leakage_source: Metadata-block ChoiceA-D +1 offset from rotation-group template. Content blocks internally consistent but EW text describes wrong topic.

DL-034_P1-E-R33.scope: Single item in Pack E. Missing CorrectChoice and Stem. Has Choices and ExplanationWrong.
DL-034_P1-E-R33.learner_impact: Cannot render a valid question. Application crash risk.
DL-034_P1-E-R33.leakage_source: Template-rotation omission — authoring template failed to populate Stem, CC, EC for this one rotation position.

total_known_certified_pool_leakage.analysis: The 89.5% v1 baseline measured leakage at certification time (items entering certification with undetected defects). Current leakage of ~6.93% in the Certified pool is lower because: (a) most pack sections have been certified clean; (b) DL-008 (539 items) resolved; (c) DL-026 (1,005 items) mostly resolved on Certified items. The remaining 154 items represent the v1 legacy that Framework v2 pre-flight gates would have caught.

v2_readiness_target_gap.current_certified_pool_leakage_pct: 6.93% (154 of 2,221 Certified items with known defects)

gap_analysis.caveat: The 6.93% figure includes only known defects. A full Gate -1 through Gate 4 re-scan of all 2,221 Certified items would likely surface additional leakage (e.g., DL-031 difficulty inflation on ~500 items, EV3 citation gaps, DL-016 on non-Section E Pack A items).
gap_analysis.true_readiness_failure_estimate: Estimated 10-15% if full retro-scan includes pedagogical defects (DL-031, EV3). Hard structural defects (DL-008, DL-026, DL-016) are concentrated in the 154 known items.

reduction_from_v1_baseline.analysis: Framework v2 does not yet exist operationally — this reduction is from manual remediation across dozens of sessions (DL-008 clear, DL-026 fills, DL-013 rewrites, certification waves). The reduction demonstrates that effective governance can achieve significant leakage reduction even without automated pre-flight gates.
